Yes, this matches how I'd expect it to work. I typed `rome AND (#article OR #book) AND NOT ancient` and only **A Weekend in Rome** stayed. That's right — the SPQR one dropped out because it's about *ancient* Rome, the pasta recipes dropped because they're neither an article nor a book, and Paris isn't about Rome at all. So the whole "this and either-of-those but not that" idea came through exactly.

Your three assumptions all line up with what I had in my head:

- Parentheses grouping the "either/or" part together is exactly how I'd read it — "(article or book)" as one bundle.
- "NOT" knocking out the thing right after it makes sense.
- And capital letters not mattering on the actual search words is what I'd want.

This is the "combining conditions" piece I asked about, and it behaves the way I imagined. 

The one remaining search thing I mentioned a couple rounds back is exact phrases in quotes — searching `"a weekend"` as that whole phrase rather than the two words separately. I don't need to see it this second, but I'll be looking for it before I'd call search fully done. For the combined AND/OR/NOT behavior you're asking about here, though, this is right.
